title: April 2025 tariff shock
sub: From the run-up to the April 2 tariff announcement to the 90-day pause a week later.

days.note: Stocks recover from an early drop on the last day of the quarter, two days before the tariff announcement.
A quiet session while markets wait for the announcement.
Stocks close higher. After the close, the US announces a 10% tariff on nearly all imports and far higher rates on about 60 countries.
The first session after the announcement: stocks, oil and the dollar fall hard.
China answers with a 34% tariff on all US goods, and stocks fall even further than the day before.
Stocks whipsaw on a false report of a pause, and the US threatens another 50% on China.
An early rally fades as the US confirms tariffs of 104% on China. Long-term yields climb.
China raises its tariffs to 84%. At 1:18 p.m. the US pauses the higher rates for 90 days for everyone but China, and stocks have their best day since 2008.
The US puts China's tariff at 145% in all, and stocks give back part of the rally.
China raises its tariffs to 125% and says it will ignore further increases. The 10-year yield ends its biggest weekly rise since 2001.

used.reason: Same emergency-cut definition, but the window runs to Dec 31, 2025, nearly eight months past the event's deadline.
used.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds an emergency meeting after which the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lowered between January 1 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An emergency meeting is defined as any unscheduled meeting called by the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) apart from the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2025.

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Federal Reserve’s website (federalreserve.gov) or credible news sources reporting on the emergency meeting.
